text: Trump says tariffs could replace your income tax. He claims they would bring in so much money that it could take the place of what Americans pay. Meet Mike. Every payday, a big piece of his check goes to income tax. So Mike loves this idea. Sounds amazing, right? Except for one number. Income tax brings in about two point seven trillion dollars a year. Tariffs? About two hundred billion last year. That's roughly thirteen times less. So to replace your income tax, tariffs would have to grow thirteen times. Overnight. And so far, no data shows that can happen. It's like paying your mortgage with your coffee money. Then came his two thousand dollar tariff checks. Asked about them, he said, when did I do that? And here's the catch. Income tax is about half of everything the government collects. Cancel it, and half the government's money vanishes. That's like Mike losing half his salary and keeping all his bills. Meanwhile, many economists say a tariff isn't paid by other countries. It's paid by the importer, and it shows up in the price tag. Mike's new TV? Higher price. His sneakers? Higher price. His car parts? Higher price. So you don't skip the tax. You just pay it somewhere else. Next time someone says no more income tax, check your receipt. Would you trade your income tax for higher prices at the store? Comment TAX or PRICES, and follow to see how money really works.
